summary: The file is not valid UTF-8, so the note is open read-only and saves its bytes unchanged.
A code fence or a $$ math block is never closed, so the rest of the note renders as code.
The property block at the top does not parse as YAML, so no property is read.
A property key is written twice, and readers disagree on which value counts.
A wikilink or Markdown link names a file that does not exist, or has no target.
An embed names a file that does not exist.
A link's #heading or #^block part names no heading or block id in its target.
Two blocks end with the same ^id, so links to it are ambiguous.
A table row has more or fewer cells than its header.
A heading is more than one level below the heading before it.
A property's value is a nested map, a block scalar, or carries comments; the engine reads it but does not rewrite it.
The file mixes line endings or has a lone CR; it is kept as it is.
More than 100 diagnostics of one code; the rest are counted, not listed.
